clue.text: Mother's about ready, prepared for fantasy

indicators.note: the mother's word goes round, sitting about the reworked letters in the middle

parts.note: a dam is an animal mother, so the mother here is DAM

indicators.note: letters that are prepared are made ready in a new order, signalling a rearrangement of ready

explanation.surface: A mother is nearly set to go, all geared up for some flight of imagination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother' is the animal sense of the word, a dam, not a human parent; 'prepared' is the anagram signal and 'about' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A daydream is a waking reverie, a pleasant imagined scene, so it is a kind of fantasy.

clue.text: Completely round article in Scottish town

parts.note: all means wholly or completely
a round shape is the letter O
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Scotland there is an article that is perfectly circular.
explanation.walkthrough: ALLOA is a small town in central Scotland, on the River Forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is the main settlement of Clackmannanshire, a place name used as the definition's example.

clue.text: Swallow drink after wind hits mountain top

parts.note: to down a drink is to swallow it
a draught is a single swallow of a drink

explanation.surface: Someone gulps a drink once the gale strikes the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like the bird, but it is the verb. The definition is a description: what comes after wind strikes a peak and spills down its lee side.
explanation.definitionFit: A downdraught is a downward current of air, typically on the lee side of a mountain once wind has crossed its summit.

clue.text: Listener's object connection with reality?

parts.note: the organ that listens is the ear
an object is a thing

explanation.surface: A question about whether something heard is truly real.
explanation.walkthrough: Earthing is the electrical connection to the ground; the question mark plays on 'earth' as solid reality, as in being down to earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthing is a wire's connection to the ground, punningly taken here as a link with the real, down-to-earth world.

clue.text: Some Fs are considered upper-class after parts of speech in trench

definitions.note: the puzzle's theme lets F stand for fat; this describes a class of fats, so the adjective stands for the noun phrase

indicators.note: the upper-class and considered pieces come after the trench piece
the parts of speech go in the trench, inside its letters

parts.note: a moat is a defensive trench round a castle
nouns are one of the parts of speech
U is the old label for upper-class usage
rated means judged or considered

explanation.surface: Certain items are deemed posh after grammar terms turn up in a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'after' order the pieces. F throughout this puzzle means fat: olive oil is the classic monounsaturated fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Monounsaturated describes fats with one double bond in the chain, such as those in olive oil, so it labels some fats.

clue.text: Turn into suit

definitions.meaning: to turn into something is to grow or change into it
to suit someone is to look good on them, as a hat may

explanation.definitionFit: Become means both to come to be something and to flatter or look right on someone.

clue.text: Second to say F from …

definitions.meaning: jocularly, someone who says 'but' and so puts the second, contrary thought
the fat taken from the next clue's beast, the cow

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs into 7 Down: the F (fat) comes from a cow. The first sense is a joke on 'but', the word that introduces a second point.
explanation.definitionFit: Butter is the fat churned from cow's milk; as a coinage, one who raises a 'but' objection.

clue.text: … beast to cause fear

explanation.definitionFit: Cow is both a farm animal and a verb meaning to frighten into submission.

clue.text: F of the sea, including ragout

annotationWithheld.why: F of the sea, including ragout (9): MARINE takes GAR, made by reading the one word 'ragout' as RAG plus 'out', so the word is both fodder and anagram indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: F of the sea, including ragout

clue.text: River following sun for "good" F

definitions.meaning: this word placed after 'sun' makes sunflower, whose oil is a healthy fat

explanation.walkthrough: A crossword river is often a 'flower', a thing that flows. Sunflower oil is the 'good' fat; F stands for fat throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a bloom, read cryptically as anything that flows, and it completes the name sunflower.

clue.text: Hush! It won't do for Scrabble then

definitions.meaning: a call for silence, asking that nothing at all be said

definitions.text: It won't do for Scrabble then
definitions.meaning: a string of letters ruled invalid in the board game is not in the dictionary

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both an instruction to keep quiet and the ruling on letters not found in the dictionary.

clue.text: F boy swallowing river

definitions.note: the puzzle's theme lets F stand for fat

indicators.note: the boy takes the river inside, swallowing it

parts.note: a lad is a boy
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A lad gulps down a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing' puts R inside LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is rendered pig fat used in cooking, so it is an example of a fat.

clue.text: Firm publication to find place to keep large instrument

parts.note: to house something is to give it room or storage
an organ is a large keyboard instrument

explanation.surface: Somebody needs to find room for a big instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A house organ is a company's in-house magazine or newsletter, a firm's own periodical.

clue.text: Ideal repose arranged for "good" F

definitions.note: a fat thought of as healthy, F standing for fat in this puzzle

indicators.note: letters that are arranged are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A perfect rest is set up for something wholesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles IDEAL REPOSE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapeseed oil, pressed from oilseed rape, is low in saturates and sold as a healthier cooking fat.

clue.text: Plains where vehicle enters nonU baths

indicators.note: the vehicle goes into the baths, entering them
non-U means without U, so the letter U is taken away

parts.note: saunas are steam baths
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: The landscape where a truck drives into common bathhouses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonU' leaves SANAS and 'enters' is the container. Non-U is also a joke on Nancy Mitford's label for lower-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Savannas are open grasslands with scattered trees, flat plains of the tropics.

clue.text: Where the Isles of Greece are revealing an age with ease

definitions.text: Where the Isles of Greece are

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are laid out to reveal something new, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: Byron's Greek islands are shown to belong to a leisurely era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealing' rearranges AN AGE and EASE; 'with' just joins them. 'The isles of Greece' opens a poem by Byron.
explanation.definitionFit: Most Greek islands lie in the Aegean, the sea between Greece and Turkey.

clue.text: Water carrier sounds off colour

indicators.note: the answer is said like the word for looking unwell

parts.note: someone off colour looks pale

explanation.surface: A water bearer seems to be feeling unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A pail is a bucket, used for carrying water.

clue.text: F with tap needing washer?

definitions.meaning: F stands for fat; this is the fat from roast meat
a tap that needs a new washer leaks drop by drop

explanation.definitionFit: Dripping is fat from roasting meat, and also leaking in drops as a worn tap does.

clue.text: Unable to wait (as they say) for a shot at top of goal

parts.note: to have a shot is to have a go

indicators.note: the top of a word in an across light is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone at a match is eager to have a crack at the top corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of' takes the first letter of 'goal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly excited, too keen to sit and wait.

clue.text: Combine to do its job, finding three Rs hard?

indicators.note: the letters are found in a new order, a cue to rearrange them

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A farm machine at work, and a schoolchild struggling with the three Rs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finding' rearranges THREE, RS and H. The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A thresher separates grain from the straw, the job a combine harvester does.

clue.text: Where to drink without food? I ask you!

indicators.note: the bar sits outside the food, holding it within

parts.note: a bar is a place to drink
an egg is a food

explanation.surface: Exasperation at a pub that serves nothing to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. The definition is someone who asks for alms.
explanation.definitionFit: A beggar asks others for money, so the begging cry 'I ask you' describes him.

clue.text: Old car to catch conductor?

parts.note: Sir Simon Rattle is a famous British conductor
to trap is to catch

explanation.surface: A banger used to ensnare a bandleader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' could be a bus conductor or electrical one, but it is Simon Rattle, the British conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattletrap is a rickety old vehicle that rattles as it goes.

clue.text: Chelsea's alternative?

indicators.note: 's here means has: the words before it hold the hidden answer

explanation.surface: A London club's other option.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'has': Chelsea has the answer inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Else means other or otherwise, offering an alternative.

clue.text: Administrators' note on Fs coming up

definitions.note: the possessive is the employees of an office collectively

indicators.note: in a down light, the note placed on the reversed fats sits after them in the entry
in a down light, coming up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: F stands for fat in this puzzle, so Fs are fats
F is a musical note

explanation.surface: A memo for managers about rising fat levels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' gives STAF; 'on' puts the note after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Staff are the people employed in an organisation, its administrators and workers.

clue.text: Set off without luggage to get French food

indicators.note: the reworked letters are outside the luggage, enclosing it
letters that are off are out of order and need rearranging

parts.note: cargo is goods carried, luggage

explanation.surface: Departing with no bags to get some French cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' gives EST, split round the luggage, which 'without' holds inside. 'Set off' looks like a departure.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargots are snails cooked as a French dish.

clue.text: Boring lot, they say

definitions.note: boring as a description of a tool's job, standing for the tool that bores

indicators.note: what they say is heard, so the word for 'lot' is spoken

parts.note: the lot is all of it

explanation.surface: People call a group dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring lot' looks like dull people, but 'Boring' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes in leather or wood.

clue.text: Where there's like pressure to weep during change of air

indicators.note: the weeping happens during, inside, the changed air
a change of letters rearranges them

parts.note: to sob is to weep

explanation.surface: Somewhere under strain, someone cries while the weather shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' gives IAR and 'during' is the container. 'like' means the same.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining places of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Fs of the west to go to Paris

definitions.note: F stands for fat, so Fs is 'Fats', the nickname of a jazz pianist

parts.note: W is the compass abbreviation for west
aller is French for 'to go'

explanation.surface: Westerners heading for France.
explanation.walkthrough: Fats Waller was the American jazz pianist and composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fats was the nickname of the jazz pianist Thomas Waller, so his surname completes the name.

clue.text: Italian magistrate keeping French boy back has a hard time

indicators.note: the magistrate holds the boy inside, keeping him

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa

indicators.note: the boy's word goes back, read in reverse

parts.note: fils is French for son

explanation.surface: A Venetian official detaining a French lad has a rough time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives SLIF and 'keeping' is the container. A doge was the elected ruler of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's life is a miserable existence, an idiom for a wretched lot.
